title: Associated log structures: construction, universal property and geometric stalks
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $R$ be a commutative monoid, and let $\beta:R\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a homomorphism to the multiplicative monoid of global regular functions. For an etale $U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] put $B_U=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and let $\beta_U:R\to B_U$ be restriction of $\beta$. The presheaf of monoids $U\mapsto R\oplus_{\beta_U^{-1}(B_U^\times)}B_U^\times$, where $(re,u)$ is identified with $(r,\beta_U(e)u)$, has a sheafification as a sheaf of commutative monoids [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. With structure map $[r,u]\mapsto\beta_U(r)u$, this sheaf $L_X(R,\beta)$ is a log structure in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with canonical map $\iota:R\to L_X(R,\beta)(X)$.

For every log structure $K$ on $X$, composition with $\iota$ is a bijection from homomorphisms of log structures $L_X(R,\beta)\to K$ over the identity of $X$ to monoid homomorphisms $v:R\to K(X)$ satisfying $\alpha_K v=\beta$. A homomorphism of log structures over the identity means a homomorphism of sheaves compatible with the maps to $\mathcal O_X$; it fixes the canonical copy of $\mathcal O_X^\times$. For every geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], writing $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and $E=\beta_{\bar x}^{-1}(A^\times)$, the canonical map $R\oplus_E A^\times\to L_X(R,\beta)_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism, compatible with $R$ and $A^\times$. For every etale $U\to X$, restriction identifies $L_X(R,\beta)|_U$ canonically with $L_U(R,\beta_U)$. A chart $R\to K(X)$ in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] identifies $K$ with this associated log structure, so the same universal property applies to $K$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, printed p. 69: associated-log and chart conventions, referring to Kato (1988), section 1. Explicit construction, universal property and stalk formula are isolated here; the underlying Kato reference is WANTED in the report.

proof.text: Put $E_U=\beta_U^{-1}(B_U^\times)$ and let $P(U)$ be the quotient of $R\times B_U^\times$ by the congruence generated by $(re,u)\sim(r,\beta_U(e)u)$ for $e\in E_U$. This is the pushout described in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]: a pair of monoid maps out of $R$ and $B_U^\times$ agreeing on $E_U$ gives the map $[r,u]\mapsto f(r)g(u)$, which respects precisely these generating relations. Restriction sends $E_U$ into $E_V$, and sends each displayed relation to the same relation over $V$, so it induces $P(U)\to P(V)$; the identity and composition laws follow on representatives. The maps $[r,u]\mapsto\beta_U(r)u$ respect the relation, multiplication and restriction, hence give $P\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$.

source.place: VI 1.1, log/chart conventions; explicit pushout quotient argument supplied by Q35

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] on the small etale site, in a universe containing its small skeleton and all coefficient sets, and set $L=P^\#$, with unit $\eta$. The same node identifies its underlying set sheaf and unit with the set sheafification. The map to the structure sheaf from Step 1 extends uniquely to a monoid-sheaf map $\alpha_L:L\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$. The maps $r\mapsto\eta_U([r,1])$ are compatible with restriction; at $U=X$ this gives $\iota$. Also $j_U(u)=\eta_U([1,u])$ defines a map $j:\mathcal O_X^\times\to L$ with $\alpha_Lj(u)=u$. The units presheaf is a sheaf: compatible units glue in the ring sheaf, and their inverses glue to its inverse.

We check the log axiom locally on sections, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] for the underlying set sheafification supplied by [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification]. Let $l\in L(U)$ have invertible image $a=\alpha_L(l)\in B_U^\times$. On a covering write $l=\eta([r,u])$. There $\beta(r)=a u^{-1}$ is a unit, so $r\in E$ and the defining relation gives $[r,u]=[1,\beta(r)u]=[1,a]$. Thus $l=j(a)$ locally and hence globally by the sheaf axiom. Conversely $\alpha_Lj(a)=a$ and this equality makes $j$ injective on every section set. Hence $j$ identifies $\mathcal O_X^\times$ with $\alpha_L^{-1}(\mathcal O_X^\times)$, exactly the log axiom of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

source.place: Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; log axiom from ILO VI 1.1

proof.text: Let $K$ be a log structure and $v:R\to K(X)$ satisfy $\alpha_Kv=\beta$. Write $j_K:\mathcal O_X^\times\to K$ for the inverse of the units isomorphism in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. On $U$ define $f_U([r,u])=v(r)|_U\,j_K(u)$. If $e\in E_U$, then $\alpha_K(v(e)|_U)=\beta_U(e)$ is a unit, so $v(e)|_U=j_K(\beta_U(e))$. Therefore $f_U([re,u])=f_U([r,\beta_U(e)u])$. The maps are monoid homomorphisms, natural in $U$, and their composites with $\alpha_K$ are the structural map of Step 1. By [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] they extend uniquely to a monoid-sheaf map $f:L\to K$. Its compatibility with the structure maps follows by uniqueness of extension to the sheaf $(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$, and $f\iota=v$.

source.place: VI 1.1 conventions; agent proof of the associated-log universal property, Kato section 1 WANTED

proof.text: Conversely let $f:L\to K$ commute with structure maps and put $v=f_X\iota$. Then $\alpha_Kv=\beta$. For a unit $u$, $\alpha_K(f(j(u)))=u$, so the units isomorphism defining the log structure forces $f(j(u))=j_K(u)$. Since $\eta_U([r,u])=\iota(r)|_Uj(u)$, $f\eta$ must be the formula of Step 4. The uniqueness clause of [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] then determines $f$ uniquely. Step 4 and this extraction are inverse, proving the stated bijection; in particular fixing units is automatic and imposes no extra hypothesis.

source.place: VI 1.1 conventions; agent verification of both inverse maps in the universal property

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$, and write $\mathcal N$ for its pointed etale neighbourhood category and $A=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N^{\mathrm{op}}}B_U$ as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], finitely many representatives or equations of germs can be realized on a common refinement: each equality in the colimit is a finite chain of restriction relations, and cofilteredness gives a common source for that chain and equalizes the finitely many parallel arrows. Consequently every $a\in A^\times$ is represented by a unit on some neighbourhood. Indeed represent $a$ and its inverse $b$ on a common neighbourhood and then refine until $ab=1$ holds there. Likewise, $\beta_{\bar x}(e)$ is a unit if and only if $e\in E_U$ on some neighbourhood: one direction is restriction, and the other applies the same inverse-and-equation argument with the fixed representative $\beta_U(e)$. No finite generation of $R$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03PQ, lemma-cofinal-etale; finite equations in the stalk colimit

proof.text: Put $Q=R\oplus_E A^\times$, with the same quotient relations, and let $P_{\bar x}$ first mean the colimit of the underlying sets of $P(U)$. The maps $[r,u]\mapsto[r,u_{\bar x}]$ respect both the quotient and restriction relations and give $\phi:P_{\bar x}\to Q$. Conversely send a representative $(r,a)$ to the germ of $[r,u]$ for any unit representative $u$ of $a$, which exists by Step 6. Two choices agree on a common refinement by the germ-equation argument there. For $e\in E$, refine further so that $e\in E_U$; then $(re,a)$ and $(r,\beta_{\bar x}(e)a)$ have images identified by the defining relation in $P(U)$. Thus this rule descends through the generated congruence to $\psi:Q\to P_{\bar x}$. Both composites fix every represented pair, so they are inverse. Multiplication on the set colimit is defined on a common refinement, is independent of choices by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], and the displayed maps preserve it and the identity. This proves an isomorphism of commutative monoids; it preserves the images of $R$ and of units by its formula.

source.place: Tag 03PQ, lemma-cofinal-etale; explicit comparison of the quotient relations in the stalk

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] to the underlying set presheaf of $P$, using [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] to identify its set sheafification with $|L|$ and its unit with $|\eta|$. It gives the bijection $P_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\bar x}$ induced by the germ of $\eta$. This is a monoid homomorphism, since $\eta$ preserves multiplication on sections and products of germs are computed on common refinements. Composing with Step 7 yields the asserted canonical $R\oplus_E A^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\bar x}$. On $R$ it sends $r$ to the germ of $\iota(r)$, and on $A^\times$ it sends a represented unit to the germ of $j(u)$, which verifies the two requested compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 03PT (2), lemma-stalk-exact, with Sites Tag 00YR underlying-set compatibility

proof.text: For etale $U\to X$, the small etale site of $U$ is the slice of that of $X$ over $U$: composition and cancellation of etale morphisms are [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and the jointly surjective covering families are the same by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On this slice, $P_X(V)=P_U(V)$ with identical quotient relations. Restriction $L_X|_U$ is a sheaf, since its covering equalizer diagrams are those of $L_X$. The underlying map $P_U\to L_X|_U$ is locally surjective and locally injective by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], applied to $P_X\to L_X$: the covering refinements of any $V\to U$ still lie over $U$. Thus [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] identifies $L_X|_U$ with the set sheafification of $P_U$. By [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification], $L_U$ is another such sheafification. The resulting canonical bijection preserves multiplication and identity, as both maps extend the same $P_U$-map, locally represented by pairs. The structure maps and the $R$-maps agree on these pairs and hence on all sections. This proves the canonical restriction isomorphism. Here $U$ is again locally Noetherian, as $U\to X$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally of finite type, and a scheme locally of finite type over the locally Noetherian $X$ is locally Noetherian by the remark in [pqf-def-locnoeth]; so $L_U(R,\beta_U)$ is a log structure on $U$ in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and Steps 1--8 apply to it.

source.place: Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification, and the local-bijection criterion; identical etale slice covering families

proof.text: Finally a chart $c:R\to K(X)$ has $\beta=\alpha_Kc$. The map $L_X(R,\beta)\to K$ of Step 4 has, by Step 8, stalk map exactly $R\oplus_{\beta_{\bar x}^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\to K_{\bar x}$, $[r,a]\mapsto c(r)_{\bar x}j_K(a)$. These are isomorphisms by the chart criterion in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For each point $x$ choose an algebraic closure of its residue field using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; by [def-weil-geometric-point] this gives a geometric point over $x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] to this covering family and the underlying set sheaves. It makes the map an isomorphism; its inverse preserves multiplication, identity and the structure map because the original map is a bijective compatible homomorphism on each section set. Transporting the bijection in Steps 4--5 across this isomorphism gives the same universal property for the charted log structure $K$.

source.place: Tag 03PU, theorem-exactness-stalks; ILO VI 1.1 chart convention
